overview: From 2025-10-01 to 2025-11-01, Sendo-labs/sendo-api had 9 new PRs (9 merged), 0 new issues, and 3 active contributors.

topContributors.summary: standujar: Drove the foundational development of several new services and plugins within the Sendo ecosystem, merging 25 pull requests this month. Their most significant contributions include bootstrapping the Sendo Analyser plugin (`plugin-sendo-analyser#1`) with over 17k lines of code and delivering the initial implementation of the Sendo Worker (`plugin-sendo-worker#1`). They also added a major X social scoring feature to the leaderboard (`leaderboard#9`) and established a comprehensive test infrastructure for the new worker plugin (`plugin-sendo-worker#2`). This activity demonstrates a strong focus on new feature development and foundational infrastructure, with work spanning application code, configuration, and tests.

Neysixx: Drove the foundational development of the `Sendo-labs/frontend` repository, establishing the initial project structure with a massive refactor in PR #1 (+17867/-16129 lines). They then built upon this foundation by implementing several core features, most notably a worker implementation in PR #2 (+8135/-3967 lines) and a chat agent in PR #13. Neysixx also addressed a critical build issue in PR #5, ensuring repository stability. Their activity shows a primary focus on large-scale refactoring and new feature development.

xdrkush: Made foundational contributions this month, most notably initializing the `sendo-api` repository in a single, large-scale effort (Sendo-labs/sendo-api#1, +21k lines). They also implemented a significant "merge-analyzer" feature on the frontend (Sendo-labs/frontend#17) and merged several PRs to fix and improve the API's "buy sell account" functionality (#3, #4) and data analysis capabilities (#6). This activity demonstrates a primary focus on bug fixes and feature development across both the API and frontend repositories.

M4XGO: Focused on establishing and rolling out automated CI/CD infrastructure across multiple repositories this month. They initiated this effort by creating reusable workflows for release management in Sendo-labs/reusable-workflows#1 (+1005/-38 lines). M4XGO then implemented these automated NPM publishing and deployment workflows across several plugins, including a significant setup in Sendo-labs/plugin-sendo-worker#3. This work was concentrated entirely on configuration and documentation files, demonstrating a strong focus on improving development operations and release processes.

0domart: Focused on implementing core feature logic in the Sendo-labs/spotlight repository this month. They landed a single, substantial pull request (Sendo-labs/spotlight#1) which completed the SOL transfer logic and added extensive unit tests. This significant contribution involved over 1500 lines of new code, with a primary focus on test-related work.

chainsona: Focused entirely on feature work, landing a single, significant pull request in the Sendo-labs/leaderboard-rewards repository (#1). This PR introduced a system to "Reward contributors" and represented a substantial effort, adding over 14,000 lines of code. The work was comprehensive, modifying 50 files and touching not just application code but also tests, configuration, and documentation.

0xCanet: Made a significant foundational contribution this month by establishing the new Sendo-labs/frontend repository. Their work consisted of a single pull request (#1), which served as the initial commit for the project. This PR was substantial, adding over 9,200 lines of code to set up the new application's initial structure.

plvo: Focused on documentation this month, contributing new materials for elizaos plugin reports in the Sendo-labs/Reports repository. Their primary contribution was merged in PR #1, which added 146 lines of new documentation. All of their activity was concentrated on documentation work.

MonteCrypto999: This month's efforts were concentrated on a single, significant feature implementation for the Sendo-labs/plugin-jupiter repository. They opened a substantial pull request (#1) to add referral fee support, which introduced over 5,900 lines of code across 31 files. This work, which is still open, primarily consisted of feature development, configuration changes, and the addition of new tests.

tionebDotsamapha: This month, tionebDotsamapha focused on improving project documentation. They contributed one pull request to Sendo-labs/sendo-api (#2), which updated the README file to English (+71/-71 lines). This activity indicates their work was entirely concentrated on documentation.

Fleo-Thyphon-ElizaOS: Made a substantial number of code changes this month, though this work has not yet been submitted for review in a pull request. They pushed 4 commits modifying 61 files, resulting in a significant volume of changes (+31328/-7996 lines). Their only other contribution was a single comment on a pull request, with their code changes indicating a focus on bug fixes and tests in addition to other work.
